svg.title: Lower and upper ten-percent tails give opposite standard normal cutoffs
svg.desc: The standard normal curve shades the lower ten percent to the left of approximately minus one point two eight two and the upper ten percent to the right of approximately plus one point two eight two. For a lower-tail probability of zero point one, Phi of z equals zero point one and z is negative. For an upper-tail probability of zero point one, the lower cumulative probability is zero point nine and z is positive. The upper-ten-percent cutoff is therefore the ninetieth percentile. Boundaries are plotted using unrounded inverse normal values and labelled to three decimal places.
